title: Grateful Dead Live at Utica Memorial Auditorium on 1973-03-21
lineage: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (Sony D8) -> M-Audio DIO 2448 -> Cool Edit Pro v1.2 -> CD -> EAC -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy 1973 Utica show captured on a solid soundboard tape with minor vocal clipping but featuring stellar Here Comes Sunshine, Dark Star and a killer Bertha opener.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its jazzy vibe, powerful second‑set jams and standout moments like Here Comes Sunshine, Dark Star > Eyes and the opening Bertha. The soundboard source is generally clear and an improvement over older copies, though several listeners note hum, vocal oversaturation and occasional clipping. Overall the show shines despite these technical quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight exceptional musical moments; recording issues are noted but not enough to outweigh the strong performance.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear with a slight tape hum and occasional vocal oversaturation/clipping; some distortion on vocals and missing few seconds of Bertha, but overall an improvement over previous versions.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong first‑set opener with Bertha followed by a flowing, jazzy second set that builds into expansive jams; audience interaction adds extra life to the performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for harmonizing on Me and Bobby McGee and tight interplay with keyboards (Slipknot riff doodle).
band_member_comments.Phil: Positive mentions of his vocal work on Box of Rain and humorous banter; no specific bass critique.
band_member_comments.Bob: Repeatedly highlighted for beautiful, louder‑in‑mix playing during Here Comes Sunshine and overall great contribution.
band_member_comments.Keys: Noted for collaborative moments with Jerry (Slipknot riff) and strong presence in jams.
